# Math

Numerics: signal processing in both domains, estimation and fitting, interpolation, statistics, randomness and units. Everything here is plain `Double`/`Float` Kotlin with no GPU and no window, so it runs in a box, a test or a headless docs capture equally well.

14 source file(s), 1287 public symbol(s). Everything below is the KDoc that lives beside the code — the same text the [completion documentation panel](../completion_doc_browser.md) shows in the editor.

| `fun ramp(start: Fn = param(0.0), end: Fn = param(1.0), domain: Domain = Domain.DEFAULT): Fn` | A **value ramp**: a straight line whose value goes from `start` to `end` as x sweeps the function's `domain`. `ramp(1.0, 6.0) over (0.0..1.0)` is 1 at x=0 and 6 at x=1; `ramp(0.0, 1.0)` is the identity over the default 0..1 domain. This is the linear sibling of `tween` (which eases the same endpoints). An unbounded domain is previewed over a finite window via `Domain.finiteSweep`, so a ramp on `Domain.ALL` stays finite to enumerate. |
| `fun ramp(start: Fn = param(0.0), end: Fn = param(1.0), domain: ClosedRange<*>): Fn` |  |

| `fun remap(from: Fn = param(0.0), to: Fn = param(1.0), domain: Domain = Domain.DEFAULT): Fn` | A **domain normalizer**: maps the x-window `[from, to]` onto `0..1`, i.e. `(x - from) / (to - from)`. `remap(0.0, 10.0)` turns an x in 0..10 into a 0..1 alpha; `remap(0.0, 1.0)` is the identity. This is the position-of-x reading — distinct from `ramp`, which produces a value that *travels* from one number to another across the domain. (Until 2026-07-14 this behaviour was misleadingly named `ramp`; it was renamed once it became clear every caller reached for `ramp` expecting the value-line semantics that `ramp` now has.) |

## spectral.kt { #spectral-kt }

Frequency-domain / spectral analysis family for the stdlib DSP toolkit.

This is the frequency-domain companion to `timeseries.kt` (which is entirely time-domain).
It is self-contained and additive: a pure-Kotlin FFT, analysis windows, a [`Spectrum`](math.md#spectral-kt-spectrum) and a
[`Spectrogram`](math.md#spectral-kt-spectrogram) (STFT), classic spectral features (centroid / spread / rolloff / flux / flatness /
RMS / energy), and streaming `FloatFilter` wrappers so the spectral features drop straight into
the existing time-domain filter chain in `timeseries.kt` (compose with `then`).

Everything is plain `Double`/`Float` math — no external DSP dependency — so it works headless in
a box, a test, or a docs capture. The FFT is an iterative Cooley–Tukey radix-2 core with a
Bluestein (chirp-z) fallback so arbitrary (non-power-of-two) lengths transform exactly.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/spectral.kt`

**Used in:** [Spectral examples](../spectral_examples.md)

### Top-level functions { #spectral-kt-functions }

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `fun fft(signal: DoubleArray, sampleRate: Double = signal.size.toDouble()): Spectrum` | Forward FFT of a real signal. `sampleRate` defaults to the signal length (bins == cycles/frame). |
| `fun fft(signal: FloatArray, sampleRate: Double = signal.size.toDouble()): Spectrum` |  |
| `fun fft(signal: List<Float>, sampleRate: Double = signal.size.toDouble()): Spectrum` |  |
| `fun fft(signal: DoubleArray, window: WindowType, sampleRate: Double = signal.size.toDouble()): Spectrum` | Windowed forward FFT: multiplies by `window` first (amplitude compensated by coherent gain). |
| `fun ifft(spectrum: Spectrum): DoubleArray` | Inverse FFT; returns the real part of the reconstructed signal. |
| `fun ifftComplex(spectrum: Spectrum): Pair<DoubleArray, DoubleArray>` | Inverse FFT keeping both real and imaginary parts. |
| `fun stft(signal: DoubleArray, fftSize: Int = 1024, hopSize: Int = fftSize / 4, window: WindowType = WindowType.HANN, sampleRate: Double = signal.size.toDouble()): Spectrogram` | Short-time Fourier transform. Frames of `fftSize` samples are windowed by `window` and advanced by `hopSize`; the tail is zero-padded so the final partial frame is kept. |
| `fun stft(signal: FloatArray, fftSize: Int = 1024, hopSize: Int = fftSize / 4, window: WindowType = WindowType.HANN, sampleRate: Double = signal.size.toDouble()): Spectrogram` |  |
| `fun stft(signal: List<Float>, fftSize: Int = 1024, hopSize: Int = fftSize / 4, window: WindowType = WindowType.HANN, sampleRate: Double = signal.size.toDouble()): Spectrogram` |  |
| `fun istft(spec: Spectrogram): DoubleArray` | Inverse STFT — weighted overlap-add reconstruction of a real signal from a [`Spectrogram`](math.md#spectral-kt-spectrogram). Each frame is inverse-transformed, re-windowed (synthesis window == analysis window) and overlap-added; the running window-energy is divided out so a Hann-windowed COLA STFT reconstructs faithfully. |
